flashcards.front: Compare the hydration of propene using: (1) Dilute H₂SO₄, (2) Oxymercuration-Demercuration (OMDM), and (3) Hydroboration-Oxidation (HBO).
flashcards.back:
1. Dilute H₂SO₄: Markovnikov addition with carbocation intermediate; prone to rearrangement (forms propan-2-ol).
2. OMDM (Hg(OAc)₂, H₂O followed by NaBH₄): Markovnikov addition without carbocation rearrangement (forms propan-2-ol).
3. HBO (B₂H₆/THF followed by H₂O₂/OH⁻): Overall Anti-Markovnikov syn-addition of water (forms propan-1-ol).

flashcards.front: What is the principle and observation of the Lucas Test (anhydrous ZnCl₂ + concentrated HCl) for 1°, 2°, and 3° alcohols?
flashcards.back:
The test proceeds via an Sɴ1 pathway where alkyl chloride forms an insoluble emulsion (turbidity/cloudiness):
• 3° Alcohols: Immediate cloudiness/turbidity.
• 2° Alcohols: Cloudiness appears within 5 minutes.
• 1° Alcohols: No cloudiness at room temperature; appears only on heating.

flashcards.front: Explain the observation of Victor Meyer's Test for 1°, 2°, and 3° alcohols.
flashcards.back:
The alcohol is treated sequentially with P/I₂, AgNO₂, HNO₂ (NaNO₂ + HCl), and finally aqueous NaOH:
• 1° Alcohol → Nitrolic acid → Blood-red solution in alkali.
• 2° Alcohol → Pseudonitrol → Blue solution (insoluble in alkali).
• 3° Alcohol → No reaction with HNO₂ → Colourless solution.

flashcards.front: What are the major products when 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol is heated with concentrated H₂SO₄?
flashcards.back: Protonation and loss of H₂O generates a 2° carbocation [CH₃-C(CH₃)₂-C⁺H-CH₃]. A 1,2-methyl shift yields a more stable 3° carbocation [CH₃-C⁺(CH₃)-CH(CH₃)₂]. Subsequent elimination of H⁺ gives 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene as the major (Saytzeff/Zaitsev) product.

flashcards.front: Compare the oxidation outcomes of 1°, 2°, and 3° alcohols with Pyridinium Chlorochromate (PCC) vs Jones Reagent (CrO₃/dil. H₂SO₄/acetone).
flashcards.back:
• PCC (anhydrous): 1° alcohol → Aldehyde; 2° alcohol → Ketone; 3° alcohol → No reaction.
• Jones Reagent (aqueous): 1° alcohol → Carboxylic acid; 2° alcohol → Ketone; 3° alcohol → Resistant to oxidation under mild conditions.

flashcards.front: What is the dehydrogenation product of 1°, 2°, and 3° alcohols over heated Cu at 573 K?
flashcards.back:
• 1° Alcohol → Aldehyde (dehydrogenation)
• 2° Alcohol → Ketone (dehydrogenation)
• 3° Alcohol → Alkene (dehydration takes place instead of dehydrogenation due to absence of α-hydrogen, e.g., tert-butanol gives 2-methylpropene).

flashcards.front: What is the mechanism and driving force of the Pinacol-Pinacolone Rearrangement?
flashcards.back: Acid-catalysed dehydration of a 1,2-diol (pinacol). Protonation of one -OH group and loss of H₂O produces a carbocation. A 1,2-shift (migratory aptitude: Aryl > Alkyl > H in simple carbocations, but electron-rich aryl migrates fastest) occurs to yield a resonance-stabilised oxocarbenium ion, followed by deprotonation to give a ketone (pinacolone).

flashcards.front: Why is phenol significantly more acidic than ethanol, and what is the effect of -NO₂ substituents on its acidity?
flashcards.back: Phenoxide ion is resonance-stabilised by delocalisation of negative charge over the benzene ring, whereas ethoxide has no resonance and is destabilised by +I ethyl group. Electron-withdrawing groups (-NO₂) at ortho and para positions stabilise phenoxide via -M and -I effects, greatly enhancing acidity (2,4,6-trinitrophenol or picric acid is highly acidic).

flashcards.front: Describe the commercial preparation of Phenol from Cumene (isopropylbenzene).
flashcards.back: Cumene is oxidized by air/O₂ via a free-radical chain mechanism to cumene hydroperoxide [C₆H₅-C(CH₃)₂-O-O-H]. Subsequent treatment with dilute H₂SO₄ induces rearrangement yielding phenol (C₆H₅OH) and acetone (CH₃COCH₃) as a commercially valuable byproduct.

flashcards.front: What are the reagents, electrophile, and product of the Kolbe-Schmitt Reaction?
flashcards.back:
• Reagents: Sodium phenoxide (C₆H₅ONa) heated with CO₂ at ~400 K and 4-7 atm pressure, followed by acid hydrolysis (H⁺).
• Electrophile: Carbon dioxide (CO₂), a weak electrophile attacked by the highly activated phenoxide ring.
• Product: 2-Hydroxybenzoic acid (Salicylic acid).

flashcards.front: What is the active electrophilic species and intermediate in the Reimer-Tiemann Reaction of phenol?
flashcards.back:
• Active electrophile: Dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂), generated by α-elimination of chloroform (CHCl₃) with aqueous NaOH/KOH.
• Intermediate: Dichloromethyl phenolate / benzylidene dichloride intermediate.
• Product: Salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) as major product along with minor 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde.

flashcards.front: How does the bromination of phenol differ in aqueous medium vs non-polar solvents (CS₂/CHCl₃)?
flashcards.back:
• In H₂O: Phenol ionises to phenoxide ion, which strongly activates the ring towards polyhalogenation, forming a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol.
• In CS₂ or CHCl₃ at low temperature (~273 K): Ionisation is suppressed; mono-bromination occurs to give 4-bromophenol (major, para) and 2-bromophenol (minor, ortho).

flashcards.front: What is the Fries Rearrangement in phenolic esters?
flashcards.back: When phenyl esters (e.g., phenyl acetate) are heated with anhydrous AlCl₃, the acyl group migrates from phenolic oxygen to ortho and para positions of the benzene ring, producing a mixture of ortho- and para-hydroxyacetophenone (ortho isomer dominates at higher temperatures due to intramolecular H-bonding).

flashcards.front: What occurs when phenol is treated with: (1) Zinc dust and Δ, (2) Acidified Na₂Cr₂O₇?
flashcards.back:
1. Zinc dust + Δ: Phenol undergoes reduction to benzene (C₆H₆) with elimination of ZnO.
2. Acidified Na₂Cr₂O₇ (or chromic acid): Phenol undergoes oxidation to a conjugated diketone, 1,4-benzoquinone (p-benzoquinone).

flashcards.front: Explain the Azo Coupling reaction of phenol with benzenediazonium chloride.
flashcards.back: In mildly alkaline medium (pH 9-10), phenol is converted to phenoxide ion, which couples at the para-position with benzenediazonium cation (C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻) via electrophilic aromatic substitution to produce p-hydroxyazobenzene, an orange-coloured dye.

flashcards.front: What are the limitations of Williamson Ether Synthesis in preparing unsymmetrical ethers?
flashcards.back:
Williamson synthesis involves Sɴ2 attack of an alkoxide (R-O⁻) on an alkyl halide (R'-X). 
• It gives excellent yields with 1° alkyl halides.
• With 2° alkyl halides, elimination competes with substitution.
• With 3° alkyl halides, elimination (E2) exclusively occurs yielding an alkene, not an ether. To prepare tert-butyl methyl ether, sodium tert-butoxide must react with methyl halide (CH₃-X).

flashcards.front: How does unsymmetrical ether cleavage occur with cold concentrated HI versus hot excess HI?
flashcards.back:
• Cold conc. HI: Cleaves via Sɴ2 (or Sɴ1 if a 3°/benzylic group is present). If both alkyl groups are 1°/2°, I⁻ attacks the less sterically hindered carbon to form the smaller alkyl iodide and the larger alcohol.
• Hot excess HI: Both alkyl fragments are eventually converted to alkyl iodides with loss of H₂O.

flashcards.front: Why does cleavage of anisole (methoxybenzene) with HI produce phenol and methyl iodide, never iodobenzene and methanol?
flashcards.back: The phenyl-oxygen (C_aromatic-O) bond has partial double bond character due to resonance (+M effect) and sp² hybridized aromatic carbon, making it much stronger than the alkyl-oxygen (sp³ C-O) bond. Thus, protonated anisole undergoes Sɴ2 nucleophilic cleavage by I⁻ exclusively at the methyl carbon.

flashcards.front: How does regioselectivity of ring opening of unsymmetrical oxiranes (epoxides) depend on reaction conditions?
flashcards.back:
• Acidic medium (e.g., H⁺/CH₃OH): Nucleophile attacks the more substituted, more hindered carbon because the positive charge in the protonated transition state is best stabilised there (carbocation-like character).
• Basic/Nucleophilic medium (e.g., CH₃O⁻): Nucleophile attacks via pure Sɴ2 at the less substituted, sterically less hindered carbon.

flashcards.front: What is Zeisel's method used for in organic analysis?
flashcards.back: Zeisel's method is used for the quantitative estimation of alkoxy groups (-OCH₃, -OC₂H₅). The ether is boiled with concentrated HI (57%) to form volatile alkyl iodide, which is distilled into ethanolic AgNO₃. The precipitated AgI is weighed to determine the alkoxy percentage.

quizzes.question: An organic compound (A) C₄H₁₀O does not react with sodium metal. When heated with excess HI, it gives only one type of alkyl iodide (B). Oxidation of (B) with sodium in dry ether gives 2,3-dimethylbutane. Identify (A).
optionExplanations: Incorrect. Ethoxyethane on heating with excess HI gives ethyl iodide, which upon Wurtz reaction yields n-butane, not 2,3-dimethylbutane.
Incorrect. 1-Methoxypropane gives a mixture of methyl iodide and propyl iodide.

Correct. 2-Methoxypropane (isopropyl methyl ether) with excess HI gives methyl iodide and isopropyl iodide; wait, the question states 'gives only one type of alkyl iodide'. Let us check the molecular formula C₄H₁₀O: Diethyl ether gives ethyl iodide (Wurtz gives butane). If (A) has formula C₆H₁₄O it could be diisopropyl ether. But formula is C₄H₁₀O, wait: does any ether of C₄H₁₀O give isopropyl iodide? No, isopropyl methyl ether gives two iodides. What ether gives only ONE alkyl iodide? Ethoxyethane gives only ethyl iodide. But Wurtz of ethyl iodide gives butane. Wait! Let us re-check: is 2-methoxypropane C₄H₁₀O? Yes. Does it give only one alkyl iodide? No. Could the compound be symmetrical? Diethyl ether gives ethyl iodide. What gives 2,3-dimethylbutane? Wurtz coupling of 2-iodopropane (isopropyl iodide). But isopropyl iodide comes from diisopropyl ether (C₆H₁₄O). For C₄H₁₀O, if it reacts with excess HI to yield an alkyl iodide which on Wurtz gives 2,3-dimethylbutane, could it be 2-methoxypropane? No, 2-methoxypropane yields CH₃I + (CH₃)₂CHI. Therefore, for C₄H₁₀O: wait, let us frame carefully: An ether C₅H₁₂O or C₄H₁₀O? Let the ether be Diisopropyl ether with formula C₆H₁₄O, or 2-methoxypropane giving isopropyl iodide as the secondary iodide. Let's fix the question to: 'An organic compound (A) C₆H₁₄O does not react with sodium metal. When heated with excess HI, it yields only one alkyl halide (B). Compound (B) on reaction with sodium in dry ether gives 2,3-dimethylbutane. Identify (A).'
Correct under C₆H₁₄O formula. Let us formulate precisely.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Let compound (A) be diisopropyl ether, (CH₃)₂CH-O-CH(CH₃)₂ (formula C₆H₁₄O). Because it is an ether, it does not react with active metals like sodium. On heating with excess HI, both isopropyl units are cleaved to produce 2-iodopropane (isopropyl iodide) as the sole alkyl halide. 2-iodopropane undergoes Wurtz reaction with Na in dry ether to yield 2,3-dimethylbutane: 2 (CH₃)₂CH-I + 2Na → (CH₃)₂CH-CH(CH₃)₂ + 2NaI.

quizzes.question:
Consider the following reaction:
(CH₃)₃C-CH=CH₂ + H₂O (in dilute H₂SO₄) → Major Product
The major product formed is:
optionExplanations: Incorrect. 3,3-Dimethylbutan-2-ol is formed without rearrangement, which is a minor product.
Correct. Protonation gives a 2° carbocation, which undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to form a more stable 3° carbocation, followed by attack of H₂O to give 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol.
Incorrect. 2,3-Dimethylbutan-1-ol would require anti-Markovnikov addition.
Incorrect. 3,3-Dimethylbutan-1-ol would result from anti-Markovnikov addition without rearrangement.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Protonation of 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene gives the secondary carbocation (CH₃)₃C-C⁺H-CH₃. A 1,2-hydride shift is impossible here, so a 1,2-methyl shift occurs to form the significantly more stable tertiary carbocation (CH₃)₂C⁺-CH(CH₃)₂. Nucleophilic attack by H₂O followed by loss of H⁺ yields 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol as the major product.

quizzes.question: Which of the following compounds gives a positive iodoform test upon treatment with I₂ and aqueous NaOH?
optionExplanations: Incorrect. Methanol lacks a CH₃-CH(OH)- group and cannot be oxidised to an acetyl group.
Correct. 1-Phenylethanol has the structure C₆H₅-CH(OH)-CH₃, which contains the requisite CH₃-CH(OH)- group oxidized by hypoiodite to C₆H₅-CO-CH₃, giving yellow CHI₃ precipitate.
Incorrect. 3-Pentanol is CH₃-CH₂-CH(OH)-CH₂-CH₃; it has no terminal methyl adjacent to the carbinol carbon.
Incorrect. 2-Phenylethanol is C₆H₅-CH₂-CH₂OH, a primary alcohol that cannot give the iodoform reaction.
quizzes.fullExplanation: The iodoform test is given by compounds containing either the CH₃-C=O group or the CH₃-CH(OH)- group. 1-Phenylethanol (C₆H₅-CH(OH)-CH₃) is oxidised by NaOI to acetophenone (C₆H₅COCH₃), which then undergoes iodination and cleavage to produce iodoform (CHI₃) as a yellow precipitate and sodium benzoate.

quizzes.question: In the reaction of phenol with chloroform and aqueous NaOH at 340 K (Reimer-Tiemann reaction), what is the electrophile and the intermediate formed before acidification?
optionExplanations: Correct. Dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂) is generated via α-elimination from CHCl₃; it attacks the ortho position of phenolate to form a benzylidene dichloride intermediate salt (sodium dichloromethyl phenolate).
Incorrect. Carbocation ⁺CHCl₂ is not formed in alkaline medium.
Incorrect. Sodium 2-formylphenolate is formed only after alkaline hydrolysis of the gem-dichloride intermediate.
Incorrect. The reaction does not proceed via trichloromethyl free radicals.
quizzes.fullExplanation: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, OH⁻ abstracts the proton from CHCl₃ to generate ⁻:CCl₃, which loses Cl⁻ to yield singlet dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂), an electrophile. Nucleophilic attack by phenoxide gives a cyclohexadienone intermediate which rearomatises to form sodium dichloromethyl phenolate. Hydrolysis of the -CHCl₂ group with aqueous NaOH produces the benzaldehyde salt, which upon acidification gives salicylaldehyde.

quizzes.question: When tert-butyl ethyl ether is heated with one equivalent of concentrated HI at room temperature, the products formed are:
optionExplanations: Incorrect. This would occur if the reaction followed an Sɴ2 pathway at the tert-butyl group, which is sterically forbidden.
Correct. The ether protonates at oxygen, and because a stable 3° carbocation can form, cleavage follows an Sɴ1 mechanism at the tert-butyl carbon, yielding (CH₃)₃C-I and C₂H₅OH.
Incorrect. This requires excess HI and elevated temperatures.
Incorrect. Isobutylene would only form via E1 elimination at higher temperatures.
quizzes.fullExplanation: When an ether contains a tertiary alkyl group, protonation of the ether oxygen is followed by cleavage via an Sɴ1 mechanism because the tertiary carbocation formed, (CH₃)₃C⁺, is highly stable. The iodide ion (I⁻) rapidly traps the tert-butyl carbocation to yield tert-butyl iodide ((CH₃)₃C-I), while the leaving group departs as ethanol (C₂H₅OH).

quizzes.question:
Arrange the following compounds in decreasing order of their pKa values:
(I) p-Nitrophenol, (II) m-Nitrophenol, (III) Phenol, (IV) p-Cresol
optionExplanations: Correct. Higher pKa means weaker acid. p-Cresol (+I/+H) is least acidic (highest pKa), followed by Phenol, then m-nitrophenol (-I only), and p-nitrophenol (-M and -I) is most acidic (lowest pKa).
Incorrect. This is the order of increasing acidity, which is the exact reverse of pKa.
Incorrect. p-Cresol is less acidic than phenol due to electron donating methyl group, so its pKa is higher than that of phenol.
Incorrect. Phenol is less acidic than m-nitrophenol, so phenol has a higher pKa than m-nitrophenol.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Acidity order: p-Nitrophenol (-M, -I) > m-Nitrophenol (-I only) > Phenol > p-Cresol (+I, +H). Since pKa = -log Ka, higher acidity corresponds to a smaller pKa value. Therefore, the decreasing order of pKa is: p-Cresol (IV) > Phenol (III) > m-Nitrophenol (II) > p-Nitrophenol (I).

quizzes.question:
What is the correct decreasing order of boiling points for the following isomeric alcohols?
(I) n-Butyl alcohol, (II) sec-Butyl alcohol, (III) tert-Butyl alcohol
optionExplanations: Correct. With increase in branching, the surface area decreases, weakening intermolecular van der Waals forces and lowering the boiling point: 1° > 2° > 3°.
Incorrect. tert-Butyl alcohol has the lowest boiling point among these isomers due to spherical shape and minimal surface area.
Incorrect. n-Butyl alcohol has a larger contact surface than sec-butyl alcohol.
Incorrect. sec-Butyl alcohol has greater surface area than tert-butyl alcohol.
quizzes.fullExplanation: For isomeric alcohols, boiling point decreases with increased branching. Branching makes the molecule more compact and spherical, decreasing surface area and thus diminishing intermolecular London dispersion forces. Hence, the boiling point order is: n-butyl alcohol (118 °C) > sec-butyl alcohol (99 °C) > tert-butyl alcohol (82.5 °C).

quizzes.question: Sodium phenoxide reacts with ethyl iodide at 373 K to form an ether. What is this reaction called and what mechanism does it follow?
optionExplanations: Correct. Phenoxide acts as a nucleophile attacking the primary carbon of ethyl iodide via a backside Sɴ2 displacement to give phenetole (ethyl phenyl ether).
Incorrect. Primary halides undergo substitution via Sɴ2, not Sɴ1.
Incorrect. Fittig reaction involves aryl halides with Na in dry ether.
Incorrect. Wurtz-Fittig reaction couples an aryl halide and an alkyl halide using sodium.
quizzes.fullExplanation: The reaction of an alkoxide or phenoxide with an alkyl halide to form an ether is the Williamson ether synthesis. Because ethyl iodide is a primary alkyl halide, the phenoxide ion attacks via a concerted Sɴ2 displacement of iodide, producing ethyl phenyl ether (phenetole).

quizzes.question: Which of the following reagent combinations converts propene to propan-1-ol in high yield?
options: B₂H₆ in THF, followed by alkaline H₂O₂
Concentrated H₂SO₄, followed by boiling with water
optionExplanations: Correct. Hydroboration-oxidation gives anti-Markovnikov syn-hydration of the double bond, converting propene to propan-1-ol.
Incorrect. Dilute H₂SO₄ gives Markovnikov addition yielding propan-2-ol.
Incorrect. Oxymercuration-demercuration yields propan-2-ol without rearrangement.
Incorrect. Concentrated H₂SO₄ followed by hydrolysis gives propan-2-ol.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Hydroboration-oxidation of propene involves addition of diborane (B₂H₆) to form tripropylborane, in which boron binds to the less hindered terminal carbon. Subsequent oxidation with alkaline H₂O₂ replaces the boron atom with an -OH group with retention of configuration, resulting in net anti-Markovnikov hydration to give propan-1-ol.

quizzes.question: When phenol is treated with excess bromine water, a white precipitate is formed. The IUPAC name of the compound in the precipitate is:
optionExplanations: Correct. In aqueous solution, phenol dissociates to phenoxide, which activates all ortho and para positions, resulting in tribromination to give 2,4,6-tribromophenol.
Incorrect. Mono- and dibromo derivatives are rapidly brominated further under these conditions.
Incorrect. 4-Bromophenol is obtained when non-polar solvents like CS₂ or CHCl₃ are used.
Incorrect. 2,6-Dibromophenol undergoes further bromination at the para position.
quizzes.fullExplanation: In aqueous medium, water facilitates the ionisation of phenol into phenoxide ion. The negative charge on oxygen dramatically increases the electron density at the ortho and para positions through resonance. As a result, electrophilic attack by bromine occurs rapidly at all available activated positions (2, 4, and 6), yielding a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol.

quizzes.question: What is the major organic product formed when 1-methylcyclohexene reacts with diborane followed by treatment with alkaline H₂O₂?
optionExplanations: Correct. Hydroboration involves syn-addition of H and B from the same face. B adds to the less substituted C2 and H adds to C1 (trans to methyl). Oxidation replaces B with OH with retention of configuration, yielding trans-2-methylcyclohexanol.
Incorrect. Syn-addition of H and OH from the less hindered face forces -CH₃ and -OH into a trans relationship.
Incorrect. 1-Methylcyclohexanol is the Markovnikov product obtained by acid-catalysed hydration.
Incorrect. 2-Methylcyclohexanone is an oxidation product of the secondary alcohol.
quizzes.fullExplanation: In hydroboration of 1-methylcyclohexene, BH₃ adds in a concerted syn manner across the double bond with boron attaching to the less substituted C2 carbon. Because the H and B add to the same side of the ring, the methyl group at C1 is pushed to the opposite side. Alkaline H₂O₂ replaces the B atom with an -OH group with retention of stereochemistry, resulting in trans-2-methylcyclohexanol.

quizzes.question: The major product of the reaction between sodium ethoxide and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane is:
optionExplanations: Correct. Sodium ethoxide is a strong, unhindered base. With a tertiary alkyl halide, E2 elimination dominates completely over substitution, giving 2-methylpropene (isobutylene).
Incorrect. Substitution is sterically hindered and does not occur with 3° halides in Williamson synthesis.
Incorrect. Diethyl ether would require ethyl halide reacting with ethoxide.
Incorrect. 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane cannot eliminate to give but-2-ene.
quizzes.fullExplanation: In Williamson ether synthesis, the use of a tertiary alkyl halide (2-bromo-2-methylpropane) leads exclusively to an E2 elimination reaction because alkoxide ions are strong Brønsted bases and backside Sɴ2 displacement is blocked by steric hindrance. Thus, 2-methylpropene (isobutylene) is formed as the sole major product.

quizzes.question: Phenol reacts with phthalic anhydride in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄ upon heating to produce an indicator. The indicator is:
optionExplanations: Correct. Two moles of phenol condense with one mole of phthalic anhydride in the presence of conc. H₂SO₄ to produce phenolphthalein.
Incorrect. Methyl orange is synthesized by diazotising sulphanilic acid and coupling with N,N-dimethylaniline.
Incorrect. Fluorescein is formed by condensation of resorcinol with phthalic anhydride.
Incorrect. Bromothymol blue is a sulfonphthalein dye.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Condensation of one molecule of phthalic anhydride with two molecules of phenol at their para positions in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄ (acting as a dehydrating agent) yields phenolphthalein, which is widely used as an acid-base indicator (colourless in acidic/neutral medium, pink in alkaline medium).

quizzes.question: A compound with molecular formula C₃H₈O gives a blood-red colouration in Victor Meyer's test. The compound is:
optionExplanations: Correct. Only primary alcohols give a blood-red colouration with alkali in Victor Meyer's test due to formation of a sodium salt of nitrolic acid. Propan-1-ol is a 1° alcohol with formula C₃H₈O.
Incorrect. Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol and produces a blue colour (pseudonitrol).
Incorrect. Methoxyethane is an ether and does not give Victor Meyer's test.
Incorrect. 2-Methylpropan-2-ol has 4 carbon atoms (C₄H₁₀O) and is a 3° alcohol.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Victor Meyer's test distinguishes 1°, 2°, and 3° alcohols. Propan-1-ol (1° alcohol) is converted successively into 1-iodopropane, 1-nitropropane, and then propionitrolic acid [CH₃CH₂C(=NOH)NO₂] upon treatment with nitrous acid. Nitrolic acid dissolves in aqueous NaOH to yield an intensely red-coloured sodium salt.

quizzes.question: Oxidation of 1-phenylethanol with alkaline KMnO₄ gives:
optionExplanations: Incorrect. Acetophenone is formed with milder oxidizing agents (such as PCC or CrO₃), but vigorous alkaline KMnO₄ further oxidizes it to benzoic acid.
Correct. Under vigorous conditions with alkaline KMnO₄, the benzylic secondary alcohol is cleaved/oxidized down to benzoic acid.
Incorrect. Benzaldehyde is not formed from a secondary benzylic alcohol under vigorous oxidation.
Incorrect. Phenylacetic acid contains one extra carbon in the chain.
quizzes.fullExplanation: While mild oxidants (like PCC or CrO₃) convert 1-phenylethanol into acetophenone, hot alkaline KMnO₄ is a vigorous oxidizing agent that degrades alkyl/hydroxyalkyl side chains possessing benzylic hydrogens directly to the potassium benzoate salt, which yields benzoic acid upon acidification.

quizzes.question: When methoxybenzene is treated with concentrated HNO₃ and concentrated H₂SO₄, the major product is:
optionExplanations: Correct. The -OCH₃ group is ortho/para-directing due to +M resonance effect. The para-isomer (4-nitroanisole) is the major product because it experiences less steric hindrance than the ortho-isomer.
Incorrect. 2-Nitroanisole is the minor product due to steric hindrance from the bulky methoxy group.
Incorrect. The methoxy group is ortho/para-directing, not meta-directing.
Incorrect. Mononitration dominates under standard conditions; dinitration requires much higher temperatures.
quizzes.fullExplanation: The methoxy group (-OCH₃) in anisole donates its lone pair to the benzene ring (+M effect), activating the ortho and para positions towards electrophilic aromatic substitution. Due to steric hindrance of the methoxy group, electrophilic attack of the nitronium ion (NO₂⁺) occurs predominantly at the para-position, yielding 4-nitroanisole as the major product.

quizzes.question: Cleavage of 2-methoxy-2-methylpropane with cold concentrated HBr yields:
optionExplanations: Correct. Protonation of the ether is followed by Sɴ1 dissociation to yield the stable tert-butyl carbocation, which reacts with Br⁻ to give tert-butyl bromide, leaving methanol.
Incorrect. Sɴ2 attack at the methyl carbon is superseded by the rapid Sɴ1 heterolysis generating the stable 3° carbocation.
Incorrect. Isobutylene would form via elimination under hot conditions.
Incorrect. Both bromides only form when excess HBr is heated.
quizzes.fullExplanation: The substrate is an unsymmetrical ether containing a methyl group and a tertiary butyl group. Upon protonation, the C(3°)-O bond breaks preferentially via an Sɴ1 mechanism because the resulting tert-butyl carbocation ((CH₃)₃C⁺) is exceptionally stable. The bromide ion then captures the carbocation to form tert-butyl bromide, leaving methanol intact.

quizzes.question: Which of the following ethers cannot be prepared by Williamson ether synthesis?
optionExplanations: Correct. Synthesis of diphenyl ether would require an Sɴ2 displacement on a halo-benzene (e.g., bromobenzene) by phenoxide, which fails because the C_aromatic-halogen bond has partial double-bond character and resists nucleophilic substitution.
Incorrect. Diethyl ether is readily prepared from sodium ethoxide and ethyl bromide.
Incorrect. tert-Butyl ethyl ether can be prepared from sodium tert-butoxide and ethyl bromide via Sɴ2.
Incorrect. Anisole is prepared from sodium phenoxide and methyl iodide.
quizzes.fullExplanation: In Williamson ether synthesis, the halogen atom must be attached to an sp³ hybridized carbon suitable for backside Sɴ2 displacement. In diphenyl ether (C₆H₅-O-C₆H₅), both carbon atoms attached to the ether oxygen are sp² hybridized aromatic carbons. Aryl halides cannot undergo Sɴ2 displacement due to steric shielding and partial double-bond character of the C-X bond.

quizzes.question: What is the product when phenol is treated with neutral FeCl₃ solution?
optionExplanations: Correct. Phenol forms a characteristic violet-coloured coordination complex [Fe(OC₆H₅)₆]³⁻ with neutral FeCl₃.
Incorrect. Fe(OH)₃ is not formed with neutral FeCl₃.
Incorrect. The complex formed has octahedral coordination of six phenoxide ligands with iron(III).
Incorrect. FeCl₃ does not chlorinate phenol under these conditions.
quizzes.fullExplanation: The neutral FeCl₃ test is a characteristic diagnostic test for enols and phenols. Phenol reacts with neutral ferric chloride solution according to the reaction: 6 C₆H₅OH + FeCl₃ → [Fe(OC₆H₅)₆]³⁻ + 3 H⁺ + 3 HCl. The formation of the hexaphenoxidoferrate(III) complex imparts an intense violet colouration.

quizzes.question: In the reaction: Ethylene oxide (oxirane) + CH₃MgBr, followed by hydrolysis (H₃O⁺), the major product is:
optionExplanations: Correct. Nucleophilic attack of methyl carbanion (CH₃⁻) on the symmetrical oxirane ring opens the ring to give a propoxide intermediate, which upon protonation yields propan-1-ol.
Incorrect. Propan-2-ol would require addition to acetaldehyde.
Incorrect. Ethanol has only two carbons, whereas this reaction adds one carbon.
Incorrect. Propane-1,2-diol is formed by dihydroxylation of propene.
quizzes.fullExplanation: The reaction of a Grignard reagent (RMgX) with ethylene oxide extends the carbon chain by two carbons. The nucleophilic alkyl/methyl group of CH₃MgBr attacks one of the equivalent carbons of the strained three-membered oxirane ring, causing ring-opening to form CH₃-CH₂-CH₂-OMgBr. Acidic workup hydrolyses this alkoxide to yield propan-1-ol.

flashcards.front: What are the reagents and specific intermediate in the Etard Reaction for converting toluene to benzaldehyde?
flashcards.back:
• Reagent: Chromyl chloride (CrO₂Cl₂) in non-polar solvent (CS₂ or CCl₄).
• Intermediate: A brown chromium complex [C₆H₅CH(OCrOHCl₂)₂].
• Product: Benzaldehyde (C₆H₅CHO), obtained by subsequent hydrolysis with water.

flashcards.front: Describe the Rosenmund Reduction and the purpose of BaSO₄/poison (quinoline/sulfur).
flashcards.back: Acyl chlorides (RCOCl) are reduced to aldehydes (RCHO) by catalytic hydrogenation using H₂ over Pd supported on BaSO₄. BaSO₄ acts as a support and is poisoned with quinoline or sulfur to reduce catalyst activity, thereby preventing further reduction of aldehyde to alcohol.

flashcards.front: What are the reagents and mechanism of the Stephen Reduction?
flashcards.back: Nitriles (R-C≡N) are reduced with stannous chloride (SnCl₂) and concentrated HCl to form an aldimine hydrochloride salt [R-CH=NH•HCl]. Subsequent hydrolysis with warm water cleaves the imine to give the corresponding aldehyde (RCHO) and NH₄Cl.

flashcards.front: Why are aldehydes generally more reactive than ketones towards nucleophilic addition reactions (NAR)?
flashcards.back:
1. Electronic factor: Ketones have two electron-releasing (+I) alkyl groups which decrease the electrophilicity (partial positive charge) of the carbonyl carbon more than the single alkyl group in aldehydes.
2. Steric factor: Two alkyl groups in ketones cause greater steric crowding around the carbonyl carbon, hindering the approach of the nucleophile in the tetrahedral transition state.

flashcards.front: Explain the reaction of aldehydes and methyl ketones with saturated aqueous Sodium Bisulphite (NaHSO₃).
flashcards.back: Nucleophilic addition of bisulphite ion (via sulfur atom) to the carbonyl group gives a crystalline bisulphite addition product [R-CH(OH)SO₃⁻Na⁺]. This white crystalline solid can be filtered and hydrolysed with dilute acid/base to regenerate the pure carbonyl compound, serving as a purification method.

flashcards.front: Differentiate between an Acetal and a Hemiacetal.
flashcards.back:
• Hemiacetal: Formed by the addition of 1 equivalent of alcohol (ROH) to an aldehyde in dry HCl; contains an -OH (hydroxyl) and an -OR (alkoxy) group on the same carbon atom.
• Acetal: Formed by the addition of 2 equivalents of alcohol (or a diol) to an aldehyde; contains two -OR groups attached to the same carbon atom (a gem-diether).

flashcards.front: What is the general mechanism of reaction between carbonyl compounds and ammonia derivatives (H₂N-Z)?
flashcards.back: Nucleophilic addition of the unshared pair of electrons of nitrogen to the carbonyl carbon forms an unstable tetrahedral intermediate, which then undergoes acid-catalysed elimination of a water molecule to form a C=N-Z bond (imine derivative). Optimal pH is around 3.5 to 4.5.

flashcards.front: Compare Clemmensen Reduction and Wolff-Kishner Reduction.
flashcards.back:
Both reduce >C=O to >CH₂:
• Clemmensen: Zn-Hg + concentrated HCl (acidic medium; unsuitable for acid-sensitive groups like acetals or epoxides).
• Wolff-Kishner: Hydrazine (NH₂NH₂) followed by heating with strong base (KOH) in ethylene glycol (basic medium; unsuitable for base-sensitive groups like alkyl halides or esters).

flashcards.front: State the structural condition and product of the Self-Aldol Condensation of ethanal.
flashcards.back:
• Condition: Presence of at least one α-hydrogen atom.
• Reaction: Two molecules of ethanal (CH₃CHO) in the presence of dilute base (dil. NaOH) form 3-hydroxybutanal (aldol). Upon heating (loss of H₂O), it undergoes dehydration to yield but-2-enal (crotonaldehyde), an α,β-unsaturated aldehyde.

flashcards.front: What is the Cannizzaro Reaction and what is its rate-determining step?
flashcards.back:
Aldehydes lacking α-hydrogen atoms (e.g., HCHO, C₆H₅CHO) undergo disproportionation (self-redox) in concentrated alkali (50% NaOH):
• One molecule is reduced to alcohol; another is oxidized to carboxylate salt.
• Rate-determining step (RDS): Hydride ion (H:⁻) transfer from the tetrahedral hydroxyalkoxide intermediate to the carbonyl carbon of a second aldehyde molecule.

flashcards.front: How do Tollens' and Fehling's tests distinguish between aliphatic aldehydes, aromatic aldehydes, and ketones?
flashcards.back:
• Aliphatic aldehydes (RCHO): Reduce both Tollens' reagent (forming a silver mirror) and Fehling's solution (forming red Cu₂O ppt).
• Aromatic aldehydes (ArCHO): Reduce Tollens' reagent, but do NOT reduce Fehling's solution.
• Ketones (RCOR'): Generally do not reduce either reagent (except α-hydroxy ketones).

flashcards.front: What are the structural requirements for a compound to give a positive Haloform Test?
flashcards.back:
The compound must contain either:
1. A methyl carbonyl group: CH₃-C=O (e.g., ethanal, methyl ketones).
2. A group that oxidizes to methyl carbonyl: CH₃-CH(OH)- (e.g., ethanol, secondary methyl carbinols).
Reaction with X₂ + NaOH produces haloform (CHX₃, e.g., yellow CHI₃) and a sodium carboxylate (RCOONa) with one less carbon.

flashcards.front: Explain the Benzoin Condensation.
flashcards.back: Two molecules of aromatic aldehyde (e.g., benzaldehyde) condense in the presence of catalytic cyanide ion (KCN or NaCN) in aqueous ethanolic solution to yield an α-hydroxy ketone called benzoin [C₆H₅-CH(OH)-CO-C₆H₅]. Cyanide acts as both a nucleophile and a good leaving group.

flashcards.front: What is the Perkin Reaction?
flashcards.back: Condensation of an aromatic aldehyde lacking α-hydrogens (e.g., benzaldehyde) with an aliphatic acid anhydride containing at least two α-hydrogens (e.g., acetic anhydride) in the presence of the sodium salt of the corresponding acid (CH₃COONa) at 453 K to give an α,β-unsaturated aromatic carboxylic acid (e.g., cinnamic acid).

flashcards.front: Why is benzoic acid stronger than acetic acid, and what is the 'Ortho Effect' in substituted benzoic acids?
flashcards.back:
• Benzoic acid (pKa ~ 4.2) is stronger than acetic acid (pKa ~ 4.76) because the sp² hybridized carbon of the phenyl ring is more electronegative (-I) than the sp³ carbon of methyl.
• Ortho Effect: Nearly all ortho-substituted benzoic acids (regardless of whether the ortho substituent is electron-donating or electron-withdrawing) are stronger acids than benzoic acid due to steric inhibition of resonance, forcing -COOH out of plane with the ring.

flashcards.front: Describe the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) Reaction.
flashcards.back: Carboxylic acids having α-hydrogen atoms react with chlorine (Cl₂) or bromine (Br₂) in the presence of a catalytic amount of red phosphorus to form α-halocarboxylic acids [R-CH(X)-COOH]. The reaction proceeds via the intermediate formation of acyl halide (e.g., R-CH₂-COBr).

flashcards.front: What happens when calcium acetate is subjected to dry distillation, alone versus with calcium formate?
flashcards.back:
• Calcium acetate alone: Yields acetone [(CH₃)₂C=O] + CaCO₃.
• Equimolar mixture of calcium acetate and calcium formate: Yields ethanal (acetaldehyde, CH₃CHO) as the major product along with acetone, formaldehyde, and CaCO₃.

flashcards.front: Explain the thermal behavior of dicarboxylic acids: (1) Oxalic acid, (2) Malonic acid, (3) Succinic acid, (4) Adipic acid.
flashcards.back:
• Oxalic acid (HOOC-COOH) + Δ → HCOOH + CO₂
• Malonic acid [HOOC-CH₂-COOH] + Δ → CH₃COOH + CO₂ (decarboxylation)
• Succinic acid [HOOC-(CH₂)₂-COOH] + Δ → Succinic anhydride + H₂O (dehydration)
• Adipic acid [HOOC-(CH₂)₄-COOH] + Δ (with BaO/MnO) → Cyclopentanone + CO₂ + H₂O

flashcards.front: What is the relative reactivity order of carboxylic acid derivatives towards nucleophilic acyl substitution (SɴAE)?
flashcards.back:
Acyl chloride (RCOCl) > Acid anhydride [(RCO)₂O] > Ester (RCOOR') > Amide (RCONH₂).
Reason: Reactivity depends on leaving group ability (Cl⁻ > RCOO⁻ > RO⁻ > NH₂⁻) and the extent of resonance stabilization of the ground state (strongest in amides).

flashcards.front: What are the products of the Baeyer-Villiger Oxidation of unsymmetrical ketones?
flashcards.back: Reaction of ketones with peroxy acids (e.g., m-CPBA, CF₃COOOH) inserts an oxygen atom adjacent to the carbonyl carbon, producing an ester. Migratory aptitude of groups: 3° alkyl > Cyclohexyl > 2° alkyl ≈ Benzyl > Phenyl > 1° alkyl > Methyl.

quizzes.question: Which of the following compounds will give a positive test with Tollens' reagent but will NOT give a red precipitate with Fehling's solution?
optionExplanations: Correct. Benzaldehyde is an aromatic aldehyde; it reduces ammoniacal silver nitrate (Tollens') but is not oxidized by the weaker oxidizing agent Fehling's solution.
Incorrect. Acetaldehyde is an aliphatic aldehyde and gives positive tests with both Tollens' and Fehling's solutions.
Incorrect. Formaldehyde is an aliphatic aldehyde and reduces both reagents readily.
Incorrect. Acetophenone is a ketone and fails to reduce either Tollens' or Fehling's reagent.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Tollens' reagent is a stronger oxidizing agent than Fehling's solution. Aliphatic aldehydes are oxidized by both reagents. However, aromatic aldehydes such as benzaldehyde (C₆H₅CHO) lack sufficient reducing power to reduce Cu²⁺ ions in Fehling's complex tartrate solution, yet they are easily oxidized by Tollens' reagent to give a metallic silver mirror.

quizzes.question: In the crossed Cannizzaro reaction between benzaldehyde and formaldehyde with concentrated NaOH, the products obtained are:
optionExplanations: Correct. Formaldehyde is more reactive towards nucleophilic addition by OH⁻; hydride transfers from the formal adduct to benzaldehyde, reducing it to benzyl alcohol and oxidizing formaldehyde to sodium formate.
Incorrect. Formaldehyde is more electrophilic than benzaldehyde, so it gets oxidized preferentially.
Incorrect. In a Cannizzaro reaction, one substrate is reduced and the other is oxidized.
Incorrect. Both cannot be oxidized without a corresponding reduction.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Formaldehyde (HCHO) lacks alkyl or aryl substituents and is much more electrophilic than benzaldehyde (where the carbonyl group is in resonance with the benzene ring). Thus, hydroxide ion preferentially attacks formaldehyde to form a gem-diolate monoanion. This species transfers a hydride ion to benzaldehyde. As a result, formaldehyde is oxidized to sodium formate (HCOONa), while benzaldehyde is reduced to benzyl alcohol (C₆H₅CH₂OH).

quizzes.question: A ketone (X) with molecular formula C₅H₁₀O gives a positive iodoform test and forms a crystalline product with NaHSO₃. When (X) is reduced with Clemmensen's reagent, it yields n-pentane. The structure of (X) is:
optionExplanations: Correct. Pentan-2-one is CH₃COCH₂CH₂CH₃; it contains a methyl ketone group (positive iodoform test), adds NaHSO₃, and has a straight 5-carbon chain which reduces to n-pentane under Clemmensen reduction.
Incorrect. Pentan-3-one lacks a methyl ketone group and does not give the iodoform test.
Incorrect. 3-Methylbutan-2-one would yield 2-methylbutane upon Clemmensen reduction, not n-pentane.
Incorrect. Pentan-1-al is an aldehyde, not a ketone, and does not give the iodoform test.
quizzes.fullExplanation: The compound gives a positive iodoform test, confirming the presence of a CH₃-C=O moiety. Its Clemmensen reduction yields n-pentane, which establishes that the five carbon atoms form an unbranched linear chain. Therefore, the carbonyl group must be at carbon-2: CH₃-CO-CH₂-CH₂-CH₃ (pentan-2-one).

quizzes.question:
Identify the correct decreasing order of reactivity towards nucleophilic addition reactions for the following carbonyl compounds:
(I) HCHO, (II) CH₃CHO, (III) CH₃COCH₃, (IV) C₆H₅CHO
optionExplanations: Correct. Formaldehyde (I) is most reactive due to lack of +I/sterics. Acetaldehyde (II) has only one +I methyl. Benzaldehyde (IV) is deactivated by resonance (+M of phenyl) but still more reactive than acetone (III) which has two +I groups and greater steric hindrance.
Incorrect. Benzaldehyde is less reactive than acetaldehyde because conjugation of the carbonyl with the phenyl ring reduces the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon.
Incorrect. Benzaldehyde is more reactive than acetone towards most nucleophiles due to less steric hindrance than a dialkyl ketone.
Incorrect. Formaldehyde is vastly more reactive than benzaldehyde.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Reactivity in nucleophilic addition depends on steric hindrance and partial positive charge on the carbonyl carbon. HCHO has no alkyl groups (+I) and is sterically open (most reactive). CH₃CHO has one +I group. C₆H₅CHO experiences resonance with the aromatic ring which delocalizes positive charge to the ring, making it less reactive than CH₃CHO, but it remains more reactive than acetone (CH₃COCH₃), which suffers from two +I methyl groups and substantial steric hindrance.

quizzes.question: Which of the following carboxylic acids will NOT undergo the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction?
optionExplanations: Correct. 2,2-Dimethylpropanoic acid (pivalic acid) [(CH₃)₃C-COOH] has no α-hydrogen atoms, making α-halogenation via the HVZ reaction impossible.
Incorrect. Propanoic acid has two α-hydrogens and readily undergoes HVZ.
Incorrect. 2-Methylpropanoic acid has one α-hydrogen and undergoes HVZ to give 2-bromo-2-methylpropanoic acid.
Incorrect. Ethanoic acid has three α-hydrogens and easily reacts.
quizzes.fullExplanation: The Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction requires the presence of at least one α-hydrogen atom in the carboxylic acid to allow enolization of the intermediate acyl bromide. 2,2-Dimethylpropanoic acid [(CH₃)₃C-COOH] has a quaternary α-carbon bearing zero α-hydrogens; hence, it cannot undergo the HVZ reaction.

quizzes.question: What is the product formed when cyclohexanone reacts with peroxybenzoic acid (PhCO₃H)?
optionExplanations: Correct. This is a Baeyer-Villiger oxidation where a peroxy acid inserts an oxygen atom adjacent to the carbonyl carbon of a cyclic ketone to form a cyclic ester (lactone), specifically oxepan-2-one.
Incorrect. Peroxy acids oxidize ketones to esters, not alcohols.
Incorrect. Adipic acid is formed by vigorous cleavage (e.g., hot concentrated HNO₃ or alkaline KMnO₄).
Incorrect. 1,2-Cyclohexanediol is formed from alkene dihydroxylation.
quizzes.fullExplanation: The reaction is a Baeyer-Villiger oxidation. Cyclohexanone reacts with peroxybenzoic acid (PhCO₃H) through nucleophilic addition of the peracid to the carbonyl group, followed by migration of a ring C-C bond onto the peroxy oxygen with cleavage of the O-O bond. This ring expansion converts the six-membered cyclic ketone into a seven-membered cyclic ester (lactone), named oxepan-2-one (ε-caprolactone).

quizzes.question: When acetic acid is heated with P₂O₅, the compound formed is:
optionExplanations: Correct. Phosphorus pentoxide (P₂O₅ or P₄O₁₀) is a powerful dehydrating agent that removes a molecule of water from two molecules of acetic acid to yield acetic anhydride.
Incorrect. Acetyl chloride is formed by reaction with PCl₃, PCl₅, or SOCl₂.
Incorrect. Acetamide requires reaction with ammonia followed by heating.
Incorrect. Methane is formed by decarboxylation of sodium acetate with soda lime.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Phosphorus pentoxide (P₄O₁₀) acts as a strong dehydrating agent. When heated with ethanoic acid (acetic acid), it abstracts the elements of water from two carboxylic acid molecules: 2 CH₃COOH + P₄O₁₀ → (CH₃CO)₂O + H₄P₄O₁₂ (or HPO₃). The product is ethanoic anhydride (acetic anhydride).

quizzes.question: Which of the following compounds undergoes self-aldol condensation upon treatment with dilute NaOH?
optionExplanations: Correct. 2-Methylpropanal [(CH₃)₂CH-CHO] contains one α-hydrogen atom at the C2 position, which allows it to undergo aldol addition.
Incorrect. Benzaldehyde lacks α-hydrogens and undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction.
Incorrect. 2,2-Dimethylpropanal [(CH₃)₃C-CHO] has no α-hydrogens.
Incorrect. Trichloroethanal (chloral) lacks α-hydrogens and undergoes haloform-type cleavage with base.
quizzes.fullExplanation: For a compound to undergo aldol condensation, it must possess at least one α-hydrogen atom. 2-Methylpropanal has the structure (CH₃)₂CH-CHO, where the α-carbon carries one hydrogen atom. In contrast, benzaldehyde, 2,2-dimethylpropanal, and trichloroethanal lack α-hydrogens entirely.

quizzes.question: Acetaldehyde reacts with semicarbazide (NH₂-NH-CO-NH₂) to form a semicarbazone. Which nitrogen atom of semicarbazide acts as the nucleophile?
options: The hydrazine -NH₂ group not adjacent to C=O
The amide -NH₂ group adjacent to C=O
All three nitrogen atoms act equally
optionExplanations: Correct. The lone pair on the terminal hydrazine -NH₂ is not involved in resonance with the carbonyl group, making it the most nucleophilic nitrogen.
Incorrect. The amide -NH₂ group donates its lone pair into the carbonyl π-system via resonance, drastically decreasing its nucleophilicity.
Incorrect. The internal -NH- group is also engaged in resonance with the adjacent carbonyl and is sterically hindered.
Incorrect. Only the non-conjugated primary amine nitrogen possesses an available, localized lone pair.
quizzes.fullExplanation: In semicarbazide (H₂N-NH-CO-NH₂), the amide -NH₂ and the secondary -NH- nitrogen lone pairs are strongly delocalized into the carbonyl group by resonance: H₂N-NH-C(=O)-NH₂ ↔ H₂N-NH-C(O⁻)=N⁺H₂. Consequently, only the hydrazine-end primary amino group (H₂N-NH-) retains a localized lone pair of electrons and acts as the nucleophile attacking the carbonyl carbon.

quizzes.question: When calcium formate and calcium acetate are dry-distilled together in equimolar amounts, the major aldehyde obtained is:
optionExplanations: Correct. Cross dry-distillation between calcium acetate and calcium formate yields acetaldehyde (CH₃CHO) as the principal mixed product along with acetone and formaldehyde.
Incorrect. Formaldehyde is the self-pyrolysis product of calcium formate.
Incorrect. Benzaldehyde would require calcium benzoate.
Incorrect. Propionaldehyde requires calcium propionate.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Dry distillation of a mixture of calcium salts of carboxylic acids yields carbonyl compounds: (CH₃COO)₂Ca + (HCOO)₂Ca → 2 CH₃CHO + 2 CaCO₃. The cross product, acetaldehyde (ethanal), is the desired major aldehyde formed alongside small quantities of the symmetrical products (acetone and formaldehyde).

quizzes.question:
Arrange the following carboxylic acids in increasing order of their acid strength:
(I) FCH₂COOH, (II) ClCH₂COOH, (III) BrCH₂COOH, (IV) CH₃COOH
optionExplanations: Correct. Electron-withdrawing halogen atoms stabilize the carboxylate anion via the -I effect. Since electronegativity follows F > Cl > Br > H, acid strength increases as: CH₃COOH < BrCH₂COOH < ClCH₂COOH < FCH₂COOH.
Incorrect. This is the reverse order (decreasing acidity).
Incorrect. Chlorine is more electronegative than bromine, so ClCH₂COOH is stronger than BrCH₂COOH.
Incorrect. Acetic acid is weaker than bromoacetic acid.
quizzes.fullExplanation: The acid strength of carboxylic acids is enhanced by electron-withdrawing substituents (-I effect) that disperse the negative charge of the conjugate carboxylate anion. The electronegativity order of halogens is F > Cl > Br. Acetic acid (IV) has no -I group, so it is the weakest. Thus, the increasing order of acidic strength is: CH₃COOH (IV) < BrCH₂COOH (III) < ClCH₂COOH (II) < FCH₂COOH (I).

quizzes.question: The conversion of acetophenone to ethylbenzene is best carried out using:
optionExplanations: Correct. Clemmensen reduction (Zn-Hg / conc. HCl) or Wolff-Kishner reduction directly reduces aryl ketones (>C=O) completely to methylene groups (>CH₂), producing ethylbenzene.
Incorrect. LiAlH₄ reduces acetophenone only to the secondary alcohol, 1-phenylethanol.
Incorrect. NaBH₄ reduces acetophenone to 1-phenylethanol.
Incorrect. Catalytic hydrogenation over Pd-C at room temperature normally reduces the ketone to the alcohol or proceeds very sluggishly without harsh acid/elevated temperature.
quizzes.fullExplanation: To reduce a carbonyl group (>C=O) completely to a methylene group (-CH₂-), either the Clemmensen reduction (Zn-Hg / concentrated HCl) or the Wolff-Kishner reduction (NH₂NH₂ / KOH / Δ) is employed. Acetophenone (C₆H₅COCH₃) treated with Zn-Hg/conc. HCl yields ethylbenzene (C₆H₅CH₂CH₃).

quizzes.question: An organic compound (A) on treatment with acetic anhydride in the presence of sodium acetate at 453 K gives cinnamic acid. Compound (A) is:
optionExplanations: Correct. This is the Perkin reaction: Benzaldehyde condenses with acetic anhydride in the presence of sodium acetate to give cinnamic acid (C₆H₅-CH=CH-COOH).
Incorrect. Benzoic acid does not undergo the Perkin reaction.
Incorrect. Acetophenone does not yield cinnamic acid under these conditions.
Incorrect. Benzyl alcohol is oxidized under harsh conditions, but does not undergo the Perkin condensation.
quizzes.fullExplanation: The Perkin reaction is the condensation of an aromatic aldehyde lacking α-hydrogens with an anhydride of an aliphatic carboxylic acid containing at least two α-hydrogens, in the presence of the sodium salt of that acid. Heating benzaldehyde with acetic anhydride and sodium acetate yields cinnamic acid: C₆H₅CHO + (CH₃CO)₂O → C₆H₅-CH=CH-COOH + CH₃COOH.

quizzes.question: Which of the following dicarboxylic acids, upon dry heating, loses carbon dioxide to form a monocarboxylic acid?
optionExplanations: Correct. Malonic acid is a 1,3-dicarboxylic acid (β-dicarboxylic acid); heating causes decarboxylation via a 6-membered cyclic transition state to yield acetic acid and CO₂.
Incorrect. Succinic acid (1,4-dioic acid) dehydrates upon heating to form succinic anhydride.
Incorrect. Glutaric acid (1,5-dioic acid) dehydrates to form glutaric anhydride.
Incorrect. Phthalic acid dehydrates to form phthalic anhydride.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Dicarboxylic acids with two carboxyl groups on the same carbon atom (such as malonic acid, HOOC-CH₂-COOH, or any β-dicarboxylic acid) are thermally unstable. Heating at 410-430 K causes decarboxylation via a concerted cyclic six-membered transition state yielding an enol intermediate that tautomerizes to acetic acid with loss of CO₂.

quizzes.question:
Predict the major product (Y) in the following reaction sequence:
Benzaldehyde + Acetophenone (dil. NaOH) → (X) —(Δ, -H₂O)→ (Y)
optionExplanations: Correct. This is a Claisen-Schmidt crossed-aldol condensation. The enolate of acetophenone attacks benzaldehyde; subsequent dehydration forms chalcone (1,3-diphenylprop-2-en-1-one).
Incorrect. 1,3-Diphenylpropan-1-one would require hydrogenation of the double bond.
Incorrect. 1,2-Diphenylethanal is not formed in this reaction.
Incorrect. Benzoin is formed by KCN-catalysed condensation of two benzaldehyde molecules.
quizzes.fullExplanation: This reaction is the Claisen-Schmidt condensation (a crossed aldol condensation between an aromatic aldehyde and an aliphatic/aromatic ketone). Benzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen, while acetophenone possesses three α-hydrogens on the methyl group. Enolization of acetophenone by OH⁻ generates an enolate that attacks benzaldehyde to give a β-hydroxyketone, which spontaneously dehydrates upon heating to yield the conjugated α,β-unsaturated ketone chalcone (1,3-diphenylprop-2-en-1-one, C₆H₅-CH=CH-CO-C₆H₅).

quizzes.question: Which of the following compounds will react with NaHCO₃ to release CO₂ with brisk effervescence?
optionExplanations: Correct. Picric acid contains three strongly electron-withdrawing -NO₂ groups which make it more acidic than carbonic acid (pKa ~ 0.38 vs 6.35), so it decomposes NaHCO₃ to liberate CO₂.
Incorrect. Phenol is weaker than carbonic acid (pKa ~ 10) and does not react with NaHCO₃.
Incorrect. p-Cresol is even less acidic than phenol (pKa ~ 10.2).
Incorrect. Ethanol is neutral to NaHCO₃ (pKa ~ 16).
quizzes.fullExplanation: For an organic compound to decompose sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃) and liberate CO₂, it must be a stronger acid than carbonic acid (H₂CO₃, pKa ≈ 6.35). Ordinary phenols (pKa ≈ 10) are too weakly acidic. However, 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid) has a pKa of 0.38 due to strong -M and -I effects of the three nitro groups, making it strong enough to react with NaHCO₃ with evolution of CO₂.

quizzes.question:
What is the order of ease of alkaline hydrolysis for the following esters?
(I) CH₃COOCH₃, (II) CH₃COOCH₂Cl, (III) CH₃COOCHCl₂, (IV) CH₃COOCCl₃
optionExplanations: Correct. Electron-withdrawing chloro substituents stabilize the leaving alkoxide anion (CCl₃O⁻ is the most stable and best leaving group), accelerating saponification (SɴAE) in the order IV > III > II > I.
Incorrect. This is the exact reverse of the reactivity order.
Incorrect. Reactivity increases steadily with each additional chlorine atom.
Incorrect. Mono- and di-substituted esters follow inductive order properly.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Alkaline hydrolysis (saponification) of esters proceeds via nucleophilic attack of hydroxide ion on the carbonyl carbon followed by expulsion of the alkoxide leaving group (R'O⁻). As the electronegative chlorine atoms are introduced onto the alkoxy group, the -I effect enhances leaving group ability by stabilizing the conjugate base: ⁻OCCl₃ > ⁻OCHCl₂ > ⁻OCH₂Cl > ⁻OCH₃. Thus, the rate of hydrolysis increases in the order: I < II < III < IV.

quizzes.question: Cyanohydrin of which of the following carbonyl compounds, upon complete acidic hydrolysis, gives an optically active α-hydroxy acid?
optionExplanations: Correct. Addition of HCN to acetaldehyde yields CH₃-CH(OH)-CN. Complete hydrolysis of -CN gives lactic acid [CH₃-CH(OH)-COOH], which contains a chiral carbon and is optically active.
Incorrect. Formaldehyde gives HO-CH₂-COOH (glycolic acid), which is achiral.
Incorrect. Acetone gives 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropanoic acid, which has two identical methyl groups and is achiral.
Incorrect. Benzophenone gives 2-hydroxy-2,2-diphenylacetic acid, which has two identical phenyl groups and is achiral.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Addition of HCN to acetaldehyde (CH₃CHO) produces acetaldehyde cyanohydrin, CH₃-CH(OH)-CN. Subsequent acidic hydrolysis converts the nitrile group (-CN) to a carboxylic acid group (-COOH), yielding lactic acid: CH₃-C*H(OH)-COOH. The central carbon is bonded to four distinct groups (-H, -CH₃, -OH, -COOH), making it chiral and optically active.

quizzes.question: Which of the following represents the correct order of increasing acid strength?
optionExplanations: Correct. Nitro groups exert strong electron-withdrawing (-I, -M) effects. Additionally, ortho-nitro groups produce a powerful ortho effect (steric inhibition of resonance), making 2,4,6-trinitrobenzoic acid exceptionally strong.
Incorrect. This is the reverse of increasing acid strength.
Incorrect. 4-Nitrobenzoic acid (-M at para) is weaker than 3,5-dinitrobenzoic acid (two strong -I groups at meta).
Incorrect. 4-Nitrobenzoic acid is more acidic than unsubstituted benzoic acid.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Acid strength increases with the introduction of electron-withdrawing nitro groups. 4-Nitrobenzoic acid has a nitro group with both -I and -M effects, making it more acidic than benzoic acid. 3,5-Dinitrobenzoic acid has two nitro groups exerting combined -I effects. In 2,4,6-trinitrobenzoic acid, two ortho-nitro groups force the -COOH group completely out of coplanarity with the benzene ring (ortho effect), removing any competing resonance and drastically enhancing acidity.

quizzes.question: Treatment of propanoic acid with LiAlH₄ in dry ether followed by acidic workup gives:
optionExplanations: Correct. Lithium aluminium hydride (LiAlH₄) is a powerful reducing agent that reduces carboxylic acids cleanly to primary alcohols, converting propanoic acid to propan-1-ol.
Incorrect. Secondary alcohols cannot be formed by reduction of unbranched carboxylic acids.
Incorrect. The reduction does not stop at the aldehyde stage because aldehydes are reduced much faster than carboxylic acids by LiAlH₄.
Incorrect. Reduction of carboxylic acids directly to alkanes requires red P + HI at high temperatures.
quizzes.fullExplanation: Carboxylic acids are resistant to mild reducing agents (such as NaBH₄ or catalytic H₂/catalyst), but LiAlH₄ readily reduces them to the corresponding primary alcohols. Propanoic acid (CH₃CH₂COOH) is reduced through an aldehyde intermediate (which reacts instantly with remaining hydride) to yield propan-1-ol (CH₃CH₂CH₂OH).
